verdict.summary: A working app installed in your own workspace takes minutes, and unlisted public distribution is self-serve with no review. But unlisted apps that are distributed commercially get 1 request/min and 15 messages per call on conversations.history/replies, can't use the Real-time Search API or the Slack MCP server, and per Slack's API terms aren't the channel for commercial distribution, so an AI agent that reads messages realistically needs a Marketplace listing (10+ active workspaces, then weeks to months of review).

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Create from manifest, install to your own workspace, copy the xoxb/xoxp token. There's no review or verification for development.

timeToProd.assumes: A Marketplace listing, which an agent that reads messages needs. Unlisted installs work the same day but are throttled.
timeToProd.waitingOn: Getting 10+ active workspaces through unlisted installs, then Marketplace preliminary review (up to 10 business days) and functional review (up to 10 weeks for new apps). Separately, each customer's workspace admin approval if their workspace restricts apps.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Review windows are Slack's stated maximums. The time to reach 10 active workspaces depends on your own go-to-market, so the total range is an estimate.

verdict.cost: Free to create and distribute apps and to submit to the Marketplace (no fee mentioned in the review docs). Semantic search via RTS needs customer plans that include Slack AI Search.

prerequisites.item: A Slack workspace where you can install apps (a free workspace or a Developer Program sandbox)
prerequisites.why: Every app is created against a development workspace, and the first install happens there.

prerequisites.item: Public HTTPS endpoints for the OAuth redirect URL and for any Events, interactivity or options-load URLs
prerequisites.why: redirect_uri must be HTTPS and match or sit under a configured Redirect URL. Public distribution requires SSL on all feature URLs.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Examples on the OAuth page mark http:// and URLs with ports as invalid. Use a tunnel such as ngrok for local development.

prerequisites.item: For Marketplace: 10+ active workspaces (used in the last 28 days, sandboxes excluded), a public landing page, privacy policy, support contact, and test credentials
prerequisites.why: These are hard prerequisites for submission. Apps below the threshold can't submit.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Discovery API security and compliance partners are exempt from the install threshold.

scopeTiers.impact: Self-serve with unlisted distribution. Enough for a bot that answers mentions and DMs via the Events API. Marketplace review still checks a justification for each scope. Apps with only bot, incoming-webhook, commands or identify scopes are generally not auto-uninstalled when the installer leaves.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: No scope requires review for unlisted apps. 'Unlisted is fine' is our reading, because the throttling applies to methods, not scopes.

scopeTiers.tier: History-reading scopes (throttled unless Marketplace or internal)
scopeTiers.impact: Installs fine, but for new commercially distributed unlisted apps conversations.history and conversations.replies drop to Tier 1 (1 request/min) with a maximum of 15 objects per call. Internal apps get 50+/min and 1,000 objects. Marketplace approval removes the throttle.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: reviewRequired=false because installing doesn't need review. In practice you need Marketplace approval to use these at agent scale.

scopeTiers.tier: Search / RTS / MCP scopes (Marketplace or internal apps only)
scopeTiers.impact: The Real-time Search API (assistant.search.context) and the Slack MCP server are not available to unlisted distributed apps. Private, IM and MPIM search need a user token. Bot-token RTS calls need an action_token from an event.
Marketplace reviewers return apps that use user tokens unnecessarily. Broad *:history user scopes need a clear use case such as real-time search or MCP. Legacy search:read is on the 'avoid' list.
Unlikely to be approved for the Marketplace unless you're in Slack's partner program.

steps.title: Get a development workspace
steps.detail: Sign in to (or create) a Slack workspace where you can install apps. A Slack Developer Program sandbox works too.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: api.slack.com/apps and api.slack.com/apps?new_app=1 returned HTTP 200 on 2026-10-19. We did not sign in.

steps.title: Draft the app manifest
steps.detail: Generate YAML/JSON with display_information, features.bot_user, oauth_config.redirect_urls (HTTPS), oauth_config.scopes.bot and .user (least privilege), settings.event_subscriptions (app_mention, message.im), and settings.token_rotation_enabled if wanted.

steps.title: Create the app from the manifest
steps.detail: Go to Create New App > From a manifest, pick the dev workspace, paste the manifest, then Create. Alternative: a human generates an App Configuration Token (valid 12h, tied to user and workspace) and an agent calls apps.manifest.create.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: You can also prefill a share link with ?new_app=1&manifest_yaml=<urlencoded>.

steps.title: Install to your own workspace and test
steps.detail: Use OAuth & Permissions > Install to Workspace. You get a bot token (xoxb-) and, if user scopes are set, a user token (xoxp-). Check it with auth.test.

steps.title: Implement the OAuth v2 install flow
steps.detail: Redirect to https://slack.com/oauth/v2/authorize?client_id=...&scope=<bot>&user_scope=<user>&state=<csrf>&redirect_uri=<https>. Exchange the code (valid 10 min) with POST https://slack.com/api/oauth.v2.access. Store the bot token per team/enterprise and the user token under authed_user. Verify state.

steps.title: Decide on token rotation before going live
steps.detail: With rotation on, access tokens (xoxe.xoxb-/xoxe.xoxp-) expire after 12h. Refresh via oauth.v2.access grant_type=refresh_token. Refresh tokens (xoxe-) are single-use, so persist the newest one. Rotation can't be turned off once enabled. It's not required for the Marketplace.

steps.title: Activate public (unlisted) distribution
steps.detail: Go to Manage Distribution and complete the checklist: HTTPS for all feature URLs, a redirect URL set, and the 'Remove Hard Coded Information' box ticked. Then click Activate Public Distribution. You get an Add to Slack button and a shareable install URL, with no review.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: Slack's docs don't list the checklist items. The 'Remove Hard Coded Information' item comes from third-party setup guides.

steps.title: Design around the unlisted-app limits
steps.detail: Ingest messages via Events (message.channels, message.groups, app_mention) instead of polling conversations.history. Paginate assuming 15 per page. Honour Retry-After on 429s. Don't plan on RTS or MCP until you're listed.

steps.title: Reach 10+ active workspaces via unlisted installs
steps.detail: Marketplace submission is blocked until the app is active in 10+ workspaces (used in the last 28 days, sandboxes excluded). Those early customers live with the throttled limits.

steps.title: Prepare Marketplace listing materials
steps.detail: Draft a per-scope justification (how you use each scope, not what it does), the landing page, a privacy policy (collection, use, retention, deletion, contact email), the support page (respond within 2 business days), and the AI disclosures (model, retention, tenancy and residency, an inaccuracy disclaimer, no LLM training on Slack data, no storing Slack data).

steps.title: Record the demo video and create test accounts
steps.detail: Record install, OAuth, setup, end-to-end use and uninstall on a non-dev workspace. Provide reviewers with test credentials for your service, with dummy data.

steps.title: Submit to the Slack Marketplace
steps.detail: Submit from the app's settings in the console, under the Marketplace submission section.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact console page name wasn't observed because we didn't sign in.

steps.title: Preliminary review
steps.detail: Covers the listing, docs, scope justifications and install access. Feedback within up to 10 business days. Your queue position resets each time you resubmit.

steps.title: Functional review
steps.detail: A reviewer installs and tests the app against the guidelines. Up to 10 weeks for new apps, up to 6 weeks for updates. Slack won't expedite for launch dates.

steps.title: Publish and manage scope changes
steps.detail: You choose when to publish after approval. The live version is locked, so adding scopes needs resubmission with a demo video. Requesting unapproved scopes returns unapproved_scope. Existing installs must reinstall to get new scopes.

agentCanDo: Write the app manifest (scopes, redirect URLs, events, token rotation)
Call apps.manifest.create / apps.manifest.update once a human provides an App Configuration Token (expires after 12h, rotate with tooling.tokens.rotate)
Implement the OAuth v2 flow, state checking, token storage and refresh handling
Build event-driven ingestion and Retry-After handling for the 15-object/1-rpm limits
Draft per-scope justifications, the privacy policy, landing page copy, support page and AI/LLM disclosures
Check endpoints (HTTPS, redirect match) and OIDC discovery for Sign in with Slack
humanMustDo: Sign in to api.slack.com and create the app or generate a configuration token
Install to the dev workspace and click Activate Public Distribution
Win 10+ active customer workspaces before Marketplace submission
Record the demo video and supply reviewer test accounts
Submit to the Marketplace, answer reviewer feedback, and click publish
Customer side: workspace owners/admins approve the app where 'Require approved apps' is on

blockers.symptom: conversations.history returns only 15 messages despite limit=200 (ok: true, non-empty next_cursor), and a second call within a minute gets ratelimited / HTTP 429 with Retry-After of about 60
blockers.cause: A commercially distributed non-Marketplace app created on or after 2025-05-29, or a new install of an existing one, is clamped to Tier 1 with a maximum of 15 objects.
blockers.fix: Get Marketplace approval, or run as an internal (single-org) app, or switch to Events API ingestion and use history only for small backfills. No parameter lifts the clamp.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The limits come from Slack's changelog. The silent clamp and 429 behaviour come from third-party write-ups.

blockers.symptom: Calls to assistant.search.context or the Slack MCP server are refused for your app
blockers.cause: RTS and MCP are limited to Marketplace-published and internal apps. Unlisted distributed apps are excluded.
blockers.fix: Get listed on the Marketplace. Until then, use your own event-driven index (subject to the ToS limits on storing data).

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: The exact error string returned wasn't documented in the pages we read.

blockers.symptom: End user can't install, or only sees a 'request to install' option
blockers.cause: The workspace owner enabled 'Require approved apps', or an Enterprise Grid org app policy is in place, which turns app approval on automatically.
blockers.fix: The user submits an approval request (if requests are enabled) and an owner or app manager approves it. Keep scopes minimal to speed this up, and give admins a security/scopes page.

evidence.label: sourced
evidence.note: There's no SLA. Approval time depends entirely on the customer's admins.

blockers.symptom: bad_redirect_uri / 'redirect_uri did not match any configured URIs'
blockers.cause: redirect_uri isn't HTTPS, has a port or a #fragment, doesn't match or sit under a configured Redirect URL, or differs between the authorize and oauth.v2.access calls.
blockers.fix: Add the exact HTTPS URL under OAuth & Permissions > Redirect URLs and send the identical value in both steps.

blockers.symptom: invalid_team_for_non_distributed_app when someone outside your workspace installs
blockers.fix: Complete the Manage Distribution checklist and activate public distribution.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: The error is listed in the OAuth docs. Mapping it to inactive distribution is our inference.

blockers.symptom: unapproved_scope during OAuth on a published app
blockers.cause: Requesting scopes the Marketplace hasn't approved yet.
blockers.fix: Submit the scope change for review (with a demo video) and only request it after approval.

blockers.symptom: Tokens stop working after about 12h, or a refresh fails with an already-used token
blockers.cause: Token rotation is enabled. Access tokens expire after 12h and refresh tokens are single-use.
blockers.fix: Refresh before expiry and atomically persist the new refresh token. Note that rotation can't be disabled.

blockers.symptom: Workspace suddenly loses the app's user-scoped access
blockers.cause: Apps with scopes beyond bot/incoming-webhook/commands/identify are auto-uninstalled when the installing user leaves or becomes a guest.
blockers.fix: Prefer bot tokens. Detect app_uninstalled/tokens_revoked events and prompt for reinstall.

nuances.text: Slack's API ToS (effective 2025-10-10) says commercial distribution needs authorization, which for most apps 'simply means submitting to our Marketplace'. The May 2025 changelog calls unlisted apps 'for development and testing—not large-scale or commercial distribution'. Unlisted distribution is a pilot channel, not a production path, for a paid product.

Existing installs of unlisted apps keep their old limits; the throttle applies to new apps and new installs. Older third-party posts cited later enforcement dates for existing installs, but the current official changelog says they are exempt.

Internal (single-organization, customer-built) apps keep Tier 3 history limits and RTS/MCP access. If your agent is deployed per customer as their own app, that sidesteps the unlisted throttle, but it has to be genuinely customer-built and internal.

evidence.label: inferred
evidence.note: Slack doesn't formally define 'internal customer-built'. Templated custom apps are called out in the ToS update as needing the Marketplace for commercial distribution.

nuances.text: AI apps on the Marketplace must not store Slack data (store metadata and fetch in real time), must not train LLMs on it, and must disclose the model, retention and residency. The API ToS also bans persistent indexes of other orgs' data obtained via the RTS/Data Access APIs and bans bulk export. This constrains RAG designs.

Bot tokens (xoxb-, scope=) act as the app. User tokens (xoxp-, user_scope=) act as the installing user. Both can come from one OAuth flow (the user token is under authed_user). Scopes are additive across reinstalls and only removable by revoking. Reviewers push back on unnecessary user tokens.
Sign in with Slack is standard OIDC (issuer https://slack.com, scopes openid/profile/email), separate from the bot/user install flow, and must be requested in its own flow.

evidence.label: tested
evidence.note: We fetched slack.com/.well-known/openid-configuration on 2026-10-19 and observed the issuer, endpoints, RS256 and the openid/profile/email scopes.

nuances.text: Turning public distribution off removes the app from every workspace except the original one. A Marketplace listing can't be un-distributed directly, only discontinued.
